items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: there was in this band was Lee Collins on trumpet Evan Hall on clarinet Alvin Morgan on bass... we used it a while... in that band was Freight Marble as leader, and the rhythm section had a fellow named Slim on drum, they had Alvin Morgan on bass, and me on banjo

ctx.x: well we didn't leave yo no with no bass that's what we left yo with so when we got there I'm gonna tell you how the band formed up we found out that Joe Wynn had been working for a guy color color named Morris which had an undertaker and he had been hiring bands over there but he was crooked with that band Joe Wynn broke away from him and got with a doctor I think the doctor was named Dr. Brunwick or something colored doctor and there was another man colored man named Aaron Long he had a meat market and Aaron…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: he took our drummer, Fat, because Al Morgan had left and went back with Feed Marlboro

ctx.x: One more question on the record. Who did the singing?

Oh yeah, the singing came about, and that came about, Alvin Morgan always could, you like to sing and scat like, looks like everybody was trying to do that, see. And Alvin could do that, so he was the one decided to say, yeah, well let me scat this, and say, let me take one on scat, you see. And I think that was supposed to be a band or solo for them, so as he did it so good, they just let it go through at that, you see. That was Alvin Morgan during the scatting, yeah. Al Morgan? Yeah, Al Morgan, yeah. His name…
Took men out of Sydney's band? Who's Sydney? Sydney Desby.
